title: Introduce invocation-signature header and kernel-queue <> token-cost correlation dashboard
author: Eleni Park
release_notes: Adds a low-cardinality invocation signature header propagated to traces and a new dashboard correlating kernel queue depth, per-token latency variance, and token-cost hotspots. No API surface breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: Long-tail latency and token-cost spikes frequently correlate with transient kernel queue saturation on Dedicated clusters and with pathological prompt shapes. This PR introduces a low-cardinality invocation signature (X-Invocation-Sig) and a first-pass dashboard that correlates kernel queue metrics with token-level latency and cost to speed RCA and automated alert tuning.

What I changed (high level):
- Add X-Invocation-Sig header generation upstream in our gateway: stable hash of (tenant_id, route, first-128-bytes-of-prompt, model_family) with a configurable salt and TTL to keep cardinality low. This header is propagated to internal request context and tracing.
- Trace enrichment: include invocation_sig as a tag/span attribute in all inference-related spans and in tenant billing traces so cost rollups can be grouped by signature.
- Metrics + exporter changes: emit kernel_queue_depth_p99_per_signature (sampled; reservoir per-signature) and token_latency_variance_per_signature as low-cardinality rollups. Added safe cardinality gating to avoid explosion (per-tenant cap + sampling).
- Dashboard: new Grafana panel group under Observability -> Inference -> Signatures that shows: kernel queue depth time series, token-latency variance sparkline, and a scatter panel overlaying token-cost (y) vs queue-depth (x) with opacity by invocation count. Also includes a small table of top-10 signatures by cost delta.
- Alerts: a new alert recipe (informational by default) that ties moderate queue-depth increases to disproportionate token cost growth for a signature over a 15m window; rule includes auto-mute if signature has <100 invocations in the window.
- Tests & e2e: unit tests for header generation and salt rotation; integration test that simulates queue saturation and asserts the signature propagates onto traces and the exporter produces one rollup metric per signature.

Why this is different from existing token-cost rollups: instead of full-token lineage or per-request high-cardinality traces, this approach intentionally creates a low-cardinality invocation fingerprint for operational grouping. It trades some exactness for signposting consistent operational patterns (prompt shards, misrouted batches, model-family hotspots) while protecting metrics storage and query performance.

Implementation notes:
- Header is generated in api/gateway (http middleware) and attached to the request context. Implementation lives in pkg/api/signature. Salt is read from config KMS-backed secret and rotated with a TTL config.
- Trace enrichment uses a small shim in the tracing library to attach invocation_sig to all subsequent spans (configurable to opt-out for Private installs).
- Metrics rollups are emitted from the serving runtime collector with a short-lived in-memory reservoir per-signature; periodically aggregated by telemetry-ingester into compact rollups in the timeseries DB.
- Dashboard JSON and panels are added under observability/dashboards/invocation-signatures.json and a migration script registers the board on deploy.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add gateway header generation and tests
- [x] Propagate signature through context + traces
- [x] Emit guarded low-cardinality metrics
- [x] Add Grafana dashboard + migration script
- [x] Add alert recipe with auto-mute gating
- [x] Manual QA on staging cluster using replaybench

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy header generation and trace enrichment to staging (opt-in via env var).
2) Enable metric rollups in telemetry-ingester in a low-rate sampling mode.
3) Deploy dashboard and preview to SRE + DX.
4) Gradually increase sampling rates for tenants with high invocation volume.

Security & privacy: The signature intentionally truncates the prompt payload to 128 bytes and is salted to avoid reconstructing user data. Private installers can disable header propagation via a single runtime flag.

Operational notes: A per-tenant cardinality cap is enforced; if exceeded the exporter emits a metric export_suppressed_by_signature_cardinality with a tag for tenant. The alert is muted automatically while suppression is active.

Testing instructions:
- Unit: run make test-packages pkg/api/signature pkg/tracing.
- Integration: run ./tools/replaybench --profile kqueue-spike --enable-signature and verify the grafana board shows the signature in the top-10 table.
- Manual: trigger a small canary on Dedicated and watch the new alert channel (observability-sig) for noisy signatures.

Related items: ENG-9420 (dashboard for kernel queue correlation), ENG-9483 (low-cardinality grouping exploration). Linked support ticket SUP-4319 reported a tenant with repeated cost spikes that motivated the pilot.
